Nitpicks: The page displays the units line as a combined string "Units: Percent, Seasonally Adjusted," while the agent output splits this into Units = "Percent" and Seasonal adjustment = "Seasonally Adjusted." This is a minor formatting difference because it preserves the exact key wording ("Percent" and "Seasonally Adjusted") and still correctly reports both required concepts.

Critical issues: None. Screenshot evidence confirms the agent was on the correct FRED series page titled "Unemployment Rate (UNRATE)" (Screenshots 1, 3, 5). The metadata shown on-page includes "Units: Percent, Seasonally Adjusted" and "Frequency: Monthly" (e.g., Screenshots 1, 3, 5), matching the agent’s reported frequency and seasonal-adjustment wording. The Observations panel screenshots clearly show the latest three displayed observations in descending order as "Aug 2026: 4.1", "Jul 2026: 4.1", and "Jun 2026: 4.2" (Screenshots 3 and 5), which exactly match the agent’s reported months and values. There is also no evidence of constraint violations (no sign-in, account creation, or subscription actions), and the agent stopped after recording the requested metadata and three latest observations, satisfying the stopping condition.

Overall, from an average user’s perspective, the agent successfully delivered the required metadata and the three latest displayed observation months/values from the correct UNRATE series page with the exact relevant wording and decimals.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to open the FRED UNRATE (Unemployment Rate) series page and accurately report (verbatim as displayed) the series metadata—units, frequency, and seasonal-adjustment wording—and the three most recent displayed observation months with their values. A reasonable user would not be flexible on using the wrong series, wrong months/values, or paraphrasing/altering the on-screen wording; they would be flexible on minor formatting such as listing seasonal adjustment on its own line if the exact wording is preserved.
